h2: Pool Repair Kuta & Legian – Leaks, Tiles & Pipework
intro: If your villa or guesthouse pool near Kuta Beach is losing water, shedding mosaic tiles, or showing rust around the fittings, Pool Repair Kuta & Legian is where to start. Most pools in these decades-old streets are now 15–20 years past their build date, so small issues tend to compound quickly. Send a few photos on WhatsApp and I'll help you decide what needs fixing first.

sections.h3: Why Pools Here Age Faster Than You'd Expect
sections.text: Salt air from the beach accelerates corrosion on ladders, skimmer baskets and metal pipe joints within a few seasons. Add low-lying lanes that flood during heavy rain—water seeps into grout lines and behind tile edges—and you get a pool that looks fine on the surface but is quietly failing underneath. In Legian especially, older guesthouses built decades ago often have original pipework still running under the pool deck. I assess all of it before recommending a fix, so you're not paying for work that isn't needed yet.

sections.h3: What I Typically Fix Around Jl. Padma & the Beachfront
sections.text: The most common calls involve slow water loss where the leak source isn't obvious—I isolate whether it's the shell, a cracked fitting, or a hidden pipe joint. Loose mosaic tiles and crumbling grout follow; salt-laden humidity works them out over time. Then there are visible pipe leaks at return jets or the drain line, which if left can soak the concrete slab beneath. For each job I explain what's urgent versus what can wait a season, so your budget goes where it matters.

sections.h3: How to Get a Quote via WhatsApp
sections.text: Open WhatsApp and send what you see—a short video walking around the pool helps enormously. Show the water level against a fixed point, any discoloured patches on tile, rust streaks near fittings, or the exact spot where drips appear. Mention how long the issue has been present and whether it worsens after rain. From those photos and notes I'll tell you what needs an in-person look and give you a clear quote before anything starts.

sections.h3: Keeping Your Pool Healthy in This Coastal Zone
sections.text: Because the air here carries salt particles that settle on every surface, rinsing metal parts with fresh water once a week makes a real difference over time. Check grout lines twice a year—especially after the wet season when flooding in Kuta's lower streets forces extra moisture into joints. Keep the skimmer basket clean so debris doesn't trap grit against the tile face. And if you run a guesthouse with multiple bathrooms upstairs, watch for slow drips at mixers; that constant seepage eventually reaches the pool deck below.

faq.q: How do I know if my pool is leaking or just evaporating?
faq.a: Evaporation drops the level evenly across the whole pool, while a leak usually shows a localized wet patch or a faster drop near one side. Send a photo of the waterline against a fixed reference point and I can help you judge from there.

faq.q: Do you handle both the pool shell issues and the plumbing behind it?
faq.a: Yes—loose tiles, grout, pipe leaks and corroded fittings are all part of the same job site, so I deal with them together rather than sending you to two different tradesmen.

faq.q: I manage a small hotel in Legian with four pools. Can you prioritise which one needs attention first?
faq.a: Absolutely. Send photos of each pool on WhatsApp and I'll rank them by urgency based on what's visible, then schedule visits accordingly.
